gaps: No attested early manuscript or excavated occurrence of 爸 itself was visually inspected. The consulted 2026 study reports a Three Kingdoms-era Guangya attestation, but this research did not establish a dated physical witness for that graph.
The phonetic classification 父 + 巴 is a source-reported analysis; no early 爸 inscription or independently inspected glyph sequence demonstrates when the compound was formed.

The origin and original depicted referent of 巴 remain disputed. The proposed animal/giant-snake reading and alternative human-figure readings are not settled; therefore the depicted object's name and pronunciation cannot be independently reconstructed here to prove a sound match.

The association of the colloquial father word with Proto-Sino-Tibetan *p/ba, and the argument that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父, are source assertions requiring specialist corroboration. The distinct reconstructions supplied use different systems and readings.

The Kangxi mirror page carrying the actual scanned entry was not text-accessible in the opened result; the entry wording was taken from a separate search-result mirror and corroborated in part by the Ministry dictionary’s cited bibliographic records.

No claim of graphic corruption or a dated sequence from oracle-bone through seal forms to 爸 is supported by the inspected evidence. The Ministry states that 爸 is absent from Shuowen; its online image references are records, not inspected glyph images.

For 巴’s component-level relation inside 爸, no distinct origin_form is asserted: 巴 is the component shape itself. Its own deeper origin is uncertain and is not transferred to 爸 as an ancestor classification.

No direct 爸 glyph image with independently established identity and reuse provenance was located. The candidates show separate component forms 父 and 巴, not the compound 爸 as an attested historical graph.
The 巴 oracle-script candidate is a modern redraw based on an image source named by Commons. It is not an excavated artifact photograph, and the page marks the period as needing specification.

The 父 oracle and seal candidates illustrate component forms only; do not use them to imply that the whole 爸 graph existed in those periods. The supplied dossier reports 爸 absent from Shuowen and no inspected early 爸 inscription.
The web tool did not expose the direct SVG image pixels, and no visual inspection is claimed. The harness should inspect the actual files before accepting captions or selection.

No usable historical image candidate for the complete graph 爸 was located in these searches. Candidate images below depict component graphs only and must not imply that 爸 existed in the Shang or seal-script periods.
The web tool could not return the 巴 and 父 oracle SVG pixels, and the 父-seal original link redirected incorrectly. No visual inspection is claimed.
The 巴 Commons page itself marks its period as needing specification; the Shang-style attribution is a source description, not a securely dated artifact identification.

No consulted source provides a securely dated physical witness for the earliest complete 爸 graph. The MOE page reports absence from Shuowen and cites earlier dictionary references, but the cited entries’ physical witnesses were not inspected here.

The formation analysis remains attributed: MOE confirms the present graphic composition 父 above 巴; Wiktionary reports 父 as semantic and 巴 as phonetic; Qiu describes 爸 as a later graph for 父 and discusses the associated sound series. These accounts do not by themselves establish when the graph was composed or settle the spoken word’s full lexical history.

The original referent/name of 巴 remains uncertain in the inspected sources. A phonetic role in 爸 and the reported historical readings do not independently identify the object depicted by early 巴 forms.

The packet’s Proto-Sino-Tibetan proposal and claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 were not independently established in this research. Do not treat this lexical-origin proposal as whole-graph borrowing or as proof of 巴’s phonetic role.

No Baxter–Sagart comparison is provided: the relevant local TSV was absent, and the inspected pages did not establish exact Baxter–Sagart rows for both 巴 and 爸. Do not mix Zhengzhang reconstructions with Baxter–Sagart notation.
